correctness.rationale: Starting uniform on one of the central dyadic cells, tau1 maps to a uniform shell of depth j with probability 2^(-j-1); tau2 switches side and enters depth 2. One-level leftward first passage of the centered (-1,+2) walk has F=z(2/3+sF^3/3), because a +2 jump requires three successive descents. Therefore H=(2z/3)/(2-F)+(zs/3)F^2. Every finite first-return itinerary is affine onto the whole return cell, preserving conditional uniformity, so excursion duration/parity pairs renew independently across returns. At z=1,s=-1, the cubic a^3+3a-2=0 gives eta=0.3564242382181135, switch prob=(1-eta)/2=0.3217878808909432; independent algebraic computation reproduced these constants. F(z,1)=1-sqrt(1-z)+O(1-z) yields 1-H=(4/3)sqrt(1-z)+O(1-z) and the nonincreasing-tail Tauberian asymptotic 4/(3sqrt(pi n)), hence infinite mean. Check is for annealed uniform entrance, not arbitrary starts.
residual_risks: Conditional uniform full-branch return assertion is essential; not claimed for deterministic initial points.
The exact return-time asymptotic follows from monotone Tauberian theorem, not finite coefficient enumeration.
